title: APA Headings: The 5 Levels With Examples | AnswerThis
summary: APA headings explained: the five APA 7 heading levels in a table, a full student paper example, the Introduction rule and setup in Word and Google Docs.
body_markdown:
APA headings divide your paper into sections, and APA 7 has five heading levels. You use them in order, starting with Level 1 for the main sections and moving down one level at a time for subsections.


Each level has its own format, so readers can see at a glance how the parts of your paper fit together. This guide shows the five levels in a table, gives a full student paper outline that uses all five, and explains how to set them up in Word and Google Docs.


## The five APA heading levels


APA Style sets one format for each level. The rules below come from the APA Style page on[headings](https://apastyle.apa.org/style-grammar-guidelines/paper-format/headings) , which follows sections 2.26 and 2.27 of the Publication Manual.


Level


Format


Where the text starts


1


Centered, Bold, Title Case


New paragraph


2


Flush Left, Bold, Title Case


New paragraph


3


Flush Left, Bold Italic, Title Case


New paragraph


4


Indented, Bold, Title Case, Ending With a Period.


Same line, after the heading


5


Indented, Bold Italic, Title Case, Ending With a Period.


Same line, after the heading


All five levels use title case, which means you capitalize the major words. They use the same font and size as the body text, and they are double-spaced like the rest of the paper.


The page below shows how each level looks in a paper.


*The five levels on a page: Levels 1 to 3 appear on their own line, while Levels 4 and 5 run into the paragraph that follows.*


## How the levels work together


Use the levels in order. Every main section gets a Level 1 heading. A subsection inside it gets Level 2, a subsection inside that gets Level 3, and so on.


Keep three rules in mind:


-


Do not skip a level. A Level 3 heading must come under a Level 2 heading.


-


Do not number or letter your headings. APA headings use format, not numbers, to show their level.


-


Avoid a single subsection. If a section has subheadings, give it at least two.

Notice the paired subsections. Participants has two Level 3 subsections, Recruitment has two Level 4 subsections and Online Sign-Up has two Level 5 subsections. APA publishes full[sample papers](https://apastyle.apa.org/style-grammar-guidelines/paper-format/sample-papers) if you want to see headings in a complete student paper. *The same outline as a tree: each step down the tree is one heading level.*


## How many heading levels to use


Use only the levels your paper needs. APA Style says the number depends on the length and complexity of the paper, and short student papers may not need any headings at all.


As a rough guide:


-


A short reflection or response paper often needs no headings.


-


A typical essay or literature review uses Level 1 and sometimes Level 2.


-


A research report with a Method section often reaches Level 3.


-


A thesis or long report may need Levels 4 and 5.


## Common headings in student papers, and the Introduction rule


Research papers in APA Style often use these Level 1 headings: Method, Results, Discussion and Conclusion. A literature review or essay uses headings that name its own topics instead.


Do not begin your paper with a heading called Introduction. APA Style treats the paper title at the top of the first page of text as a de facto Level 1 heading, so the introduction comes right after it with no extra heading. Our guide to the[APA title page](https://answerthis.io/blog/apa-title-page) shows the page that comes before this one, and our guide to the[research paper introduction](https://answerthis.io/blog/research-paper-introduction) explains what the opening section should cover.


If you need a correct title page fast, the AnswerThis[APA title page generator](https://answerthis.io/apa-title-page-generator) formats a student title page with the title, author, affiliation, course, instructor and due date. It is free, uses no AI and needs no signup. It does not make a professional title page or a reference list.


## Heading examples for common student papers


The Level 1 headings change with the type of paper. The table gives typical choices. Your instructor’s assignment sheet may ask for other headings, so follow it first.


Type of paper


Typical Level 1 headings


Research report or lab report


Method, Results, Discussion


Literature review


One heading for each theme, such as Screen Use Before Bed, Sleep Duration and Academic Outcomes


Case study


Case Description, Analysis, Recommendations


Argumentative essay


One heading for each main point, then Conclusion


Under each Level 1 heading, add Level 2 headings only where a section has two or more distinct parts.


## How to set up APA headings in Word and Google Docs


Built-in heading styles save time and keep every heading consistent. They also build an outline you can use to move around your paper.


### 1. Set up Heading 1 to Heading 3 as styles


In Word, open the Styles group on the Home tab, right-click Heading 1 and choose Modify. Set the font to match your body text, make it bold and black, center it and set the spacing before and after to 0 pt with double line spacing. Repeat for Heading 2 (flush left, bold) and Heading 3 (flush left, bold italic).


In Google Docs, format one heading the APA way, select it and choose Format, Paragraph styles, then Update Heading 1 to match. Repeat for Heading 2 and Heading 3.


### 2. Type Levels 4 and 5 as part of the paragraph


Levels 4 and 5 start on the same line as their paragraph, so a separate heading style does not work well. Instead, indent the paragraph and type the heading in bold (Level 4) or bold italic (Level 5), end it with a period and keep typing.


### 3. Check your structure in the outline


In Word, turn on the Navigation Pane from the View tab. In Google Docs, open the document outline from the View menu. The outline shows your Level 1 to Level 3 headings in order, which makes a skipped level easy to spot.


### 4. Check your citations and references


Headings organize the paper, but your citations need care too. The AnswerThis[APA citation generator](https://answerthis.io/apa-citation-generator) creates APA 7 author-date citations from source details or details you enter yourself, and the first 3 sources are free. Check the authors, dates and DOI links before you use them. If a source is a PDF, our guide on[how to cite a PDF](https://answerthis.io/blog/how-to-cite-a-pdf) shows how to find its source type first.


To draft a full section, such as a literature review with citations in APA Style, follow our tutorial on how to[write a section](https://answerthis.io/guide/steps-to-write-a-section-using-answerthis) in AnswerThis.


## Common mistakes


-


Starting the paper with an Introduction heading. The paper title already does this job.


-


Skipping a level, such as putting a Level 3 heading straight under a Level 1 heading.


-


Numbering headings, such as “1.0 Method” or “A. Participants”.


-


Adding blank lines above or below headings. APA Style says not to, even when a heading falls at the end of a page.


-


Formatting Levels 4 and 5 as separate lines. Their text continues on the same line.


## Conclusion


APA headings are a map of your paper. Pick the levels your paper needs, use them in order, and let format, not numbers, show the structure. Set them up once as styles, and every heading after that will follow the rules on its own.


For a wider look at the two most common student styles, see our comparison of[APA vs MLA](https://answerthis.io/blog/apa-vs-mla) .


## FAQs


### How many heading levels are there in APA 7?


There are five. Level 1 is centered and bold, Level 2 is flush left and bold, Level 3 is flush left in bold italic, and Levels 4 and 5 are indented and run into the paragraph.


### Is Introduction a heading in APA Style?


No. Do not begin a paper with an Introduction heading. The paper title at the top of the first page of text works as the heading for the introduction.


### Are APA headings bold?


Yes. All five levels are bold. Levels 3 and 5 are also italic.


### Can you skip heading levels in APA?


No. Use the levels in order. A Level 3 heading must come under a Level 2 heading, which must come under a Level 1 heading.


### Do APA student papers need headings?


Not always. Short student papers may not need any headings. Longer papers, such as research reports, use them to separate the main sections.
